correctness.rationale: A fixed unordered pair determines a unique locally constant H→C2 interchange character; the trivial sector is UConf_2(F) for the H-fixed subtree F, nontrivial χ has kernel K and is (X^K\F)/C2 via x↦{x,gx}. Finite-group isometric fixed sets of a tree are nonempty convex subtrees. An involution with fixed subtree F cannot preserve any component of X^K\F: the midpoint of a segment joining x and gx would be a fixed point inside that component. Branch pairs are homeomorphic to open contractible subtrees, and UConf_2(F) for nondegenerate F is connected with free rank β(F)=∑_v binom(deg_F(v)-1,2) in H1 by the two-strand Farley–Sabalka cell count. F a singleton gives empty trivial sector. Pair-count and no higher homology follow. The theorem is for unordered two points only and uses geometric, not only vertex, fixed sets.
